Tidy comparison of forecast scores across mvgam models

Source: R/compare_scores.R
compare_scores.Rd

Bundles per-series-per-horizon scores from several mvgam_forecast objects into one long-format tibble, with one row per model x series x horizon combination. For joint scores ("energy", "variogram", "twenergy") the per-series scores are NA and the joint score is the row with series == "all_series".

Usage

compare_scores(..., score = "crps", model_names = NULL, score_args = list())

Arguments

...

Two or more mvgam_forecast objects (the same shape score.mvgam_forecast() consumes). Argument names are taken from the call and used as the model column. Bare expressions like compare_scores(fc1, fc2) produce model levels "fc1" and "fc2".

score

Character. Which proper scoring rule to evaluate. Forwarded to score.mvgam_forecast(); see its documentation for the supported values.

model_names

Optional character vector of model labels; overrides the names inferred from the call.

score_args

Optional named list of extra arguments passed to score.mvgam_forecast() (for example score_args = list(interval_width = 0.6)).

Value

A tibble with columns:

  • model – factor with one level per supplied forecast.

  • series – factor of series names (plus an "all_series" level when a joint score is requested).

  • eval_horizon – integer horizon within the test window (1, 2, ...).

  • score – the requested score value.

  • in_interval – coverage indicator carried through from score.mvgam_forecast().

See also

score.mvgam_forecast(), plot.mvgam_compare_scores(), compare_elpds(), forecast.mvgam(), ensemble.mvgam_forecast()

Other forecasting: ensemble.mvgam_forecast(), forecast.mvgam(), hindcast.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), score.mvgam_forecast()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(1)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
# Two models of one count series: a smooth of x with and without
# an AR(1) trend
mod_gam <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), data = simdat$data_train,
                 family = poisson(), chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 25 of 2000 (1.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
mod_ar <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
                data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
                chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
# }
# \dontrun{
fc_gam <- forecast(mod_gam, newdata = simdat$data_test)
fc_ar <- forecast(mod_ar, newdata = simdat$data_test)

# One row per model and horizon, scored by the discrete ranked
# probability score (lower is better)
scores <- compare_scores(fc_gam, fc_ar, score = "drps",
                         model_names = c("GAM", "AR"))
summary(scores)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 4
#>    series   eval_horizon   GAM    AR
#>    <fct>           <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 series_1            1  1.62  1.09
#>  2 series_1            2  3.20  1.71
#>  3 series_1            3  7.72  5.58
#>  4 series_1            4  7.15  6.36
#>  5 series_1            5 11.6   5.82
#>  6 series_1            6  6.38  3.04
#>  7 series_1            7  1.32  1.08
#>  8 series_1            8  1.81  1.32
#>  9 series_1            9  4.29  2.47
#> 10 series_1           10  2.11  1.70
#> # ℹ 20 more rows

# The AR model's DRPS minus the GAM's. Negative values favour the
# AR model
plot(scores, relative = "GAM")


# Next, ensemble() combines the two forecasts
# }
